Foundry Task Kit

The parts the task screens are built from, and the rules for placing them. Foundations feed primitives, primitives make components, components take slots, slots sit in a pattern's regions, and a pattern, or no pattern, makes a task screen.

Tier 1

Foundations

The decisions every primitive inherits. Carbon’s White/Gray 10 theme for light, Gray 100 for dark, IBM Plex, the 2x grid. The shell header stays dark in both themes, as in Carbon’s UI shell.

How components are placed

Slots

A slot is the job a component does on this screen. Ask in this order; the first yes is the slot. The same component can take another slot on another screen.

OrderAskSlotComponents that took it (measured)
1Does it name the task and whose move it is?task_headertask-header
2Does it choose what the workspace shows: search, filters, a list you pick an item from?query_controlsfilter-bar work-queue
3Is it the commit, or something you enter or choose that travels with it?action_areaai-insight ending-picker confirm-dialog recipient-list form-section answer-composer
4Does it show what is wrong, missing or about to happen?validation_feedbackreceipt change-summary message-preview evidence-list rule-checks
5Is it where the work itself is done?primary_workspacework-queue record-summary comparison-table bulk-review-table offer-ladder share-bar scenario-controls kpi-tile bar-compare findings-checklist slot-planner weighbridge-reading line-capture scan-field form-section expiry-runway duplicate-check
6Is it facts about the subject: what it is, why it is here, its history?context_panelrecord-summary rule-checks activity-thread signal-list scorecard-table timeline evidence-list
7Is it figures that inform the choice?supporting_analysisexposure-meter signal-list trend-chart comparison-table scorecard-table cover-check scenario-compare capacity-bar
8Is it background you could do without?secondary_contextactivity-thread
9Does it move between stages?step_navigationstep-nav
How components are placed

Placement rules

Inside a region, components follow step order, top to bottom. These rules then decide neighbours and what stays in view; the higher rule wins. Every example below is written in a task's screens.json.

1

The main work gets the largest region

  • Procurement T7 The charts take the main column: interpreting the measures is the work
  • Stores T1 The planner takes the main column: placing lorries is the work
2

What is compared together stays visible together

  • Credit T1 The endings sit beside the exposure and the payment signals the reason quotes, and stay pinned while those scroll
  • Credit T2 Hold or leave open sits beside the DSO trend and the limit used, which the reason quotes
  • Credit T3 What has gone and what has not sits in the main column, beside the request its reason is written from
  • Credit T6 The answer is written beside the customer’s figures, with each fact one click away
  • Procurement T1 Approve, return or reject sits beside the rate comparison and the vendor’s record
  • Procurement T6 The options sit right under the share controls, so moving a slider changes the comparison in view
  • Procurement T12 The tests sit under the rate comparison they are answered from
  • Stores T1 Crew hours and KA-QC space sit beside the planner and change as lorries are placed
  • Stores T2 The PO and the challan sit left of the entry, read as the paper would be
  • Stores T12 The closest items sit directly under the description they were found from, so the two can be compared
  • Stores T16 The cover check sits beside the quantity and need-by date it tests
3

A warning sits next to what it is about

  • Credit T4 Each row’s Ready or Open status sits at the end of that row, not in a summary elsewhere
  • Procurement T1 Each risk point sits next to the rule that gave it
  • Procurement T7 Missing measures are named beside the concerns they limit, never drawn as zero in the charts
  • Stores T2 The 200 kg warning sits inside the PO line it is about, not in a banner
  • Stores T2 · phone The 200 kg warning stays inside the PO line, even on a phone, and comes again in the last view
  • Stores T11 Each batch’s runway sits inside its own row
  • Stores T12 The gate's message sits under the check it is about, not at the top of the page
  • Stores T16 The order-by warning sits under the cover check it comes from
4

The commit sits at the point of decision

  • Credit T1 Each ending names where it goes: Nisha for approve, Arun for reject or hold
  • Credit T2 Who is told sits right above the endings, because the notice goes with the press
  • Credit T3 Usha is named as the receiver right above the send
  • Credit T4 What will go to Teja sits right above the send
  • Credit T6 Send sits under the answer and names SO-2 as where it is kept
  • Procurement T5 The preview sits directly above the endings, because Send sends exactly that message
  • Procurement T6 The recommendation sits beside the vendors’ figures it is argued from
  • Procurement T12 The conclusion sits beside the PO’s timeline
  • Stores T2 The endings sit under the hand-overs they cause
  • Stores T2 · phone The endings come last, right after the hand-overs they cause
  • Stores T11 What the actions will start sits right above Close the check
  • Stores T12 The send sits beside the summary of what will be sent
5

Background goes lowest

  • Credit T1 The conversation with Sales is background, so it sits last in the evidence column
  • Procurement T5 The vendor conversation is background, so it sits last in the main column
6

Fit the device

  • Stores T2 · phone The desk's three columns become one, in region order; the split is into views, not smaller columns
How a task is shown

One screen or several

One screen is the default; 14 of the 16 plans use one. A task splits only for a stated reason. Keep together what is compared, revisited, or changed by another step; split for an order gate, a device that cannot show what must be seen together, sustained focus, or a change of mode.
